transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-20
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (CTO, Quantum Analytics), Sofia Martinez (ML Eng), Ben Cho (DevOps)

Summary:
- POC scoping focused on integration planning: using Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs, function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs, benchmarks and timelines.
- Customer success criteria: p95 latency < 300ms for typical 256-token responses, throughput ~200 req/s at steady state, cost target <$0.02 per 1k tokens for gen workload, no PII retention and SOC2 compliance.
- Tentative 4-week POC timeline; Redwood to provide SDK examples and benchmark harness; customer to provide prompts and infra access.

Topics:
- Integration points: REST/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs (python/node), streaming vs non-streaming, function-calling, tool integration.
- Benchmarks: p95/p99, throughput, tokenization, batching impacts, KV cache/ prefix caching.
- Security: VPC peering, KMS, audit logs, retention, SOC2, SSO.
- Success criteria and go/no-go decision points.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, we wanted to run through the POC scope and specifically the integration checklist. I'm Maya, AE on the account.
[00:12] Ravi: Hi Maya, thanks, I'm Ravi, CTO at Quantum Analytics. Sofia and Ben are here too. We're mostly interested in an easy migration from our current OpenAI-compatible calls and running a performance benchmark.
[00:22] Sofia: Yeah hi, uh, thanks. Our main thing is we have a user-facing assistant that averages ~256 tokens per response and peak concurrent sessions around 60-80. We want to avoid any big latency regressions.
[00:35] Liam: Great, that helps. Quick question on current stack, Sofia: are you using the official OpenAI SDK today or a homegrown client?
[00:42] Sofia: We're using the OpenAI python SDK v0.28 for generation and a custom wrapper for function calling.
[00:49] Maya: Perfect — Redwood exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and we also provide first-class SDKs for python and node that map almost 1:1. We'll send sample snippets but generally your existing calls should work with minimal changes.
[01:05] Ben: For networking, we're on AWS in us-west-2. We need VPC peering and allowed IPs, we can't route traffic through public internet for PII workloads.
[01:15] Liam: Understood. We support VPC peering and we can provide an allowlist of egress IPs; for Private deployments we can do a private control plane as well. For the POC, peering plus TLS+KMS is usually sufficient.
[01:28] Ravi: Ok good. On success criteria, we want p95 latency under 300ms for gen calls with payload size around 256 tokens and p99 under 450ms, cost under $0.02 per 1k tokens — is that realistic?
[01:44] Liam: Those are tight but we can get there with model selection and batching. For hosted Redwood we can configure batching and prefix/KV cache to reduce per-token cost; for dedicated we can guarantee throughput and lower tail latencies. We'll test both a larger model and a quantized variant to see tradeoffs.
[02:05] Sofia: Can you explain the KV cache bit? I've seen notes about prefix caching but not in depth.
[02:12] Liam: Sure. With repeated prefixes and session-based contexts we keep the key-value cache warm so subsequent calls skip recomputing early layers — it effectively reduces compute per token. In practice we see 20-40% cost decrease for conversational workloads with lots of reuse. Apologies, sometimes the transcript shows it as "K-V cash" in our docs.
[02:33] Ravi: Makes sense. For the POC workload we'll prepare a 5k prompt set representative of production and run a 10k sample generation for benchmarks.
[02:43] Maya: Great. Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — integration + smoke tests; Week 1 — benchmark runs at concurrency levels (8, 32, 64); Week 2 — cost and quality analysis; Week 3 — decision and handoff. So about 4 calendar weeks.
[03:02] Ben: On the integration, does Redwood support function/tool calling as OpenAI does? We have several tools that the model calls for inventory lookup and order status.
[03:14] Liam: Yes, we support function calling semantics and also structured JSON output modes; we also have tool calling abstractions if you want decoupled tool exec. Your existing wrapper should adapt to our endpoints; we have example SDK code that demonstrates registration of functions and returning typed JSON.
[03:30] Sofia: Any caveats on streaming? We rely on streaming for token-wise UI updates.
[03:36] Liam: Streaming is supported. In some high-concurrency scenarios streaming can slightly increase server-side CPU due to connection handling, but we can tune pool sizes. We recommend testing both streaming and non-streaming runs in the benchmark.
[03:52] Maya: We'll also provide a benchmark harness — a simple locust/jmeter-like script that can simulate your 60-80 peaks and measure p95/p99, throughput and cost per token.
[04:03] Ravi: Can you run on our data or do we need to sanitize it? We have some sensitive PII in transcripts.
[04:12] Maya: For initial runs we can run on redwood hosted with data-in-transit encrypted; we do not persist any PII by default for POC unless you opt in. For stronger controls we can enable customer-managed encryption keys and private deployments.
[04:26] Ben: We'll need SOC2 docs and a security questionnaire answered.
[04:31] Maya: Absolutely — I'll attach the SOC2 attestation and our security pack. Expect a security questionnaire link from our security team by EOD.
[04:40] Sofia: On model parity and quality, we need a blind eval vs our baseline — say 500 samples graded for correctness.
[04:48] Liam: We can run the eval and produce a quality report; we'll also hook up your existing eval harness if you share the test set. We'll report metrics like exact match, F1, hallucination rate where applicable.
[04:59] Ravi: How long to set up the benchmark? From Redwood side how long will it take to spin up dedicated capacity if needed?
[05:07] Liam: For the POC, integration + smoke deploy is usually 1-2 business days. Spinning dedicated capacity can be done within a week given resource availability — we'll note that in timeline as optional step after initial benchmarks.
[05:18] Ben: Are there any client library differences that will break our telemetry or observability hooks?
[05:24] Maya: No major differences — we expose headers and tracing hooks. The SDKs propagate request ids and provide per-token cost estimates. We'll include a sample with opentelemetry header mapping.
[05:36] Sofia: One more thing: tool calling — can we run synchronous calls with a guaranteed time budget? Some of our tools are slow.
[05:44] Liam: We support sync tool calls with timeouts and async callbacks. For slow tools we recommend async tool execution with model receiving a tokenized placeholder and then resuming once the tool returns.
[05:58] Ravi: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:02] Maya: Recap — Redwood to send SDK samples (python/node), benchmark harness, SOC2/security docs, and an allowlist for VPC. Quantum to upload the 5k prompt set, share a sample eval set, and confirm test windows. We'll schedule the benchmark the week of 2027-03-01.
[06:20] Ben: Sounds good.
[06:22] Sofia: Yup.
[06:25] Ravi: Thanks everyone.
